newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank caps zloty, lifts key market rate.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank caps zloty, lifts key market rate.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the currency basket nudged down by small-scale interventions by the central bank, which bought a symbolic $4 million on the interbank market at 3.0708 and 3.0713 zlotys, dealers said.

They said the central bank sent a signal to the market not to venture past the three percent from parity rate resistance after the zloty inched up ignoring the dollar's gains against the mark on international markets.
"The zloty ignored the dollar's gains as there was an upward pressure because of foreign supply of currencies...and the central bank stepped in," said Piotr Nowak from BPH SA.
Analysts said that NBP decided to raise market rates in order to keep its monetary policy sufficiently tight.
"NBP is probably not happy with the rate of decline in credit growth and it decided to raise short term market rates and flatten the yield curve at 22 percent," said Elwir Swietochowski from PBI SA.
After the move the yield curve for all NBP instruments was flat for maturities ranging from two weeks to nine months.
O/N rates were at 22.40/22.60 percent, up from opening's 22.10/22.30 percent and T/N were at 22.45/22.65 percent, up from 22.15/22.45.
